# Review, pass 1 — secret-history-191-193 (§§191–193)

Reviewer: adversarial pass 1. Read: conventions.md, runbook.md, packet.md, units.json, the pilot (secret-history-01-06.json), the published 189-190 units, run3 RUNBOOK §2, and (for glossary cross-checks only) known-forms.json / novel-forms.json. No modern translations, no web.

Unit numbers below are 1-based (unit 1 = "Belgütei nojan-u …", unit 72 = "keġežü iležüġüi."), the same numbering the notes use ("unit 12" = oroγulba). `t` and word order untouched; edits were made by script (units.json kept in its original indent-1 layout).

Checks that passed with no change: every `t` equals the packet words of its index run; 72 units, 392 words, indices 0–391 once each, in order; every Ming gloss in brackets on each word matches the packet gloss for that index; the supplied and printed quotation marks (printed: close after boltuγai, open at "Dalan, close at adqun, open at "Oorčin, close at qonotuγai, open and close around Moṅγol-un … ažuγu, close at bolqu-ju, open at "Tein, close at tüleġülüdkün, close at üžežü (treated as stray, said so), close at bi twice; supplied ones are each announced in a note); house renderings (Qahan/Qan, Chinggis, Kerülen, Jebe, "issued a decree:", groom, geldings, Belgütei Noyan, Arqai-Qasar, Tayang).

### Medium (sense, label or lemma wrong)

It is an active causative: the night guards make their own standing ones stand, parallel to kebteġülžü in unit 23. · l → "let-them-make-stand"; i → "and set their standing ones to stand at the door in turn."; n corrected and the accusative (i) of baiqun(i)- named as the object.

## Findings refused (with reason)

- Unit 29 i drops "their own days" (üdür(i)-jen): l carries it, and the English "the three nights and three days of the shift" is the sense; adding it makes the sentence worse.
- Unit 71 i (aqun-u): l has a question mark, i is a statement. The note already says the question reading is open; the glossary's aqun-u is "perhaps, may it not be", so neither is secure. Left.
- Units 69/72 ile-: i keeps "going to him / they went". Ming 去了 supports "went"; the glossary's "send" rests on a different Ming (敎去了). Both are flagged in the notes; not forced.
- Unit 38 "with Jebe and Qubilai, the two, as vanguard": English "with X as vanguard" means X is the vanguard, which is the accusative's force. Kept.
- Unit 57 čadumu-že "will be full": the present ending is itself uncertain, and the whole speech is a plan. Kept.
- Unit 2 i "held a circle hunt": the note already says baγu- + aba is uncertain. Kept.
- qadqul- (stem) against a possible qadqu- + -ldu-: cannot be settled from the Ming and the Shiratori text alone. Left.
- čeri + -ġüd (glossary: čerig): both segmentations fit; the glosser can reconcile the lemma. Left.
- Three labels for -kün/-qun (participle "one who", imperative plural, future participle "shall do"): different words by Ming gloss and syntax; accepted as homographs.
- Süiketü / Abjiya / Qanghar-Qan spellings in i: no house form, no source to check against beyond Shiratori; kept.
- Notes' numbering of "units" (1-based): checked at every cross-reference, all correct; no change.

## For the glosser / pass 2 (known entries that do not cover this part's use)
aba (known entry is a- + -ba "dwelt"; here the noun "circle hunt", Ming 圍獵); tüšižü (known "stretch out the neck", here tüši- "entrust, appoint", Ming 委付着); adqun (known adqu- "grip, seize" Ming 拿着; here Ming 住着, a- + -d- + -qun); čiležü (known "call, summon"; here "be weary", Ming 困乏着); žailažu (known "hide, avoid" Ming 躱; here Ming 挪着); turγaγ(ud) (known "bodyguard", Ming 護衞; here Ming 散班 and, once, 宿衞); ileġed / iležüġüi (known "send"); Ornuγ̇u (known "a mountain", here Ming 地名); manaγar (known Ming 早行, here 明早行); tedüi (known entry already has 便; here 卽便 and 那些 both covered); an-u / min-u / in-ü morph lemmas now match the published parts.
